chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Hadrami, from Al-Kahili, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man whose mother married him while he was absent.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage is valid. If the groom wishes, he may accept it; and if he wishes, he may reject it. So if the groom rejects the marriage arranged for him, the dowry remains obligatory upon his mother.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mother marries her absent adult son without his prior consent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the fiqh of 'tazwij al-walidayn' (parental marriage of an adult child), establishing that while the contract is initially valid, it remains subject to the son's ratification (ikhtiyar). Scholarly tradition interprets this as a balance between parental authority and individual autonomy, ensuring that if the son exercises his right to reject the match, the financial burden of the dowry (mahr) reverts to the mother who initiated the arrangement.
